title: Tunnels & Vehicle Fires
whatItIs: Tunnels reduce visibility, so keep a bigger gap. If your vehicle catches fire, get everyone out to a safe place and call the fire brigade.
keyFacts: At night or in poor visibility, don't wear tinted glasses or visors if they restrict your vision.
Keep at least a two-second gap in a tunnel.
If you have to stop in a tunnel, leave at least a 5-metre gap to the vehicle in front.
Breakdown or incident: hazard lights on, then keep well away from your vehicle and moving traffic.
Engine fire anywhere: get everyone out to a safe place and call 999. Don't open the bonnet.

items.title: Stop safely
items.text: If you can, stop in a place of relative safety and switch off the engine.

items.title: Hazard lights on
items.text: Use your hazard warning lights to warn other traffic.

items.title: Get everyone out
items.text: Get the occupants out quickly and to a safe place.

items.title: Keep the bonnet shut
items.text: Don't try to put out an engine fire: opening the bonnet will make it flare.

items.title: Call the fire brigade
items.text: Call 999 with the exact location. Wait well away from the vehicle and traffic.

a.label: Gap in a tunnel
points: Moving: at least a two-second gap

b.label: Engine fire
points: Get everyone out to a safe place

onTheTest.question: You have to stop in a tunnel. What gap should you leave to the vehicle in front?
onTheTest.why: Leave at least a 5-metre gap when you stop in a tunnel. When moving, keep at least a two-second gap.

traps: Stopping in a tunnel? Leave at least a 5-metre gap to the vehicle in front.
Don't try to put out an engine fire: opening the bonnet will make the fire flare.
Tinted glasses or visors that restrict your vision: not at night or in poor visibility.
